compare_digimon.description: Put two Digimon side by side and say what they have in common: the levels, types, attributes and fields they share, and any evolution that appears in both their lines. Both profiles come back whole, so a step can report the differences as easily as the overlap. Useful for a matchup post, a quiz, or deciding whether two Digimon are related at all.

first.description: An Armor-level Insect Digimon which evolved through the power of the "Digimental of Knowledge". The "Digimental of Knowledge" has the attribute of "Earth", and those that don this Digimental wield the power to manipulate the earth.
first.name: Digmon

second.description: An Armor-level Insect Digimon which evolved through the power of the "Digimental of Knowledge". The "Digimental of Knowledge" has the attribute of "Earth", and those that don this Digimental wield the power to manipulate the earth.
second.name: Armadimon

get_attribute.description: Get one attribute by name or ID, as the encyclopedia records it. Useful for resolving an attribute name that came from somewhere else into the exact spelling a search filter takes.

parameters.description: The attribute's name or ID (for example, Vaccine or 4). Run List attributes to see them all. A Digimon's own attributes can be referenced straight from an earlier step; where one hands over several, the first is looked up.
parameters.name: attribute

get_digimon.description: Get everything the encyclopedia records about one Digimon: its artwork, every level, type, attribute and field it belongs to, its release year, its reference-book profile in English and Japanese, every skill it attacks with, and what it evolves from and into. Takes a name or an ID, so a name read from a message or a spreadsheet can be looked up directly.

get_digimon_profile.description: The same Digimon, flattened to the handful of fields a post, a card or a message actually needs: name, artwork, levels, types, attributes, fields, release year, skill names, evolutions, and the reference-book text in one language. Saves a workflow digging through the full record for the two fields it wanted. Falls back to whatever language the entry does have and says so, since many entries are Japanese only.

get_evolution_line.description: Follow a Digimon's evolutions outwards and return everything the walk reaches, grouped by how many steps away it is. One record only names its immediate neighbours, so this is what turns 'what does Armadimon become' into the whole branch. Choose the direction and how many steps to take; each Digimon is reported once however many paths reach it, and the conditions the encyclopedia records come along with it.
get_evolution_line.display_str_template: Trace the evolution line of Digimon {0}.
get_evolution_line.name: get_evolution_line

parameters.description: The Digimon to start from, by name or ID (for example, Armadimon or 271).
parameters.name: digimon

parameters.description: Whether to follow what this Digimon evolves into, what it evolves from, or both.
parameters.name: direction

options.label: Forwards, to what it evolves into
Backwards, to what it evolves from

parameters.description: How many evolution steps to follow out from the starting Digimon. Two covers a Digimon and what its evolutions become; the lines fan out quickly, so a deep walk is slow. Up to 4.
parameters.name: depth

depth.description: How many steps the walk actually reached.

stages.description: One entry per step out, each holding the Digimon reached at that distance.

total_count.description: How many Digimon the walk reached in total.

truncated.description: True when the walk hit its lookup ceiling and there is more line beyond what is here.

description: Look up Digimon using the free, keyless Digimon API (DAPI): search the encyclopedia by name, level or attribute, get a Digimon's full record or a flattened profile ready to post, draw a random one, trace an evolution line out to its branches, compare two Digimon, and browse the levels, attributes, types, fields and skills behind it all. No account and no API key required. Disclaimer: this is an independent integration with the community-run Digimon API (digi-api.com).
